name: BT Halftoner
changelog:
0.2.2

  • Smallest dot now starts at 0.8 mm. On the pressed test sheets nothing under 0.7 mm was reliable and 0.8 mm was a lot better, so that is the new starting point.
  • Lines per inch now starts at 15 (dots about 1.7 mm apart). 0.8 mm dots need that much room to grow from small to large; at the old 25 a fade jumped almost straight from scattered dots to solid.
  • If you never changed those two sliders, you get the new values automatically. Anything you set yourself is kept.

0.2.1

  • Defaults set from the shop's own test print. Dots 0.5 mm and up held clean on the shirt; anything smaller broke up. Holes under about 0.6 mm filled in. So Smallest dot stays at 0.5 mm and Smallest gap now starts at 0.6 mm (was 0.4), which means the darkest part of a fade goes solid a little sooner instead of printing holes that plug.

0.2.0

  • Dot sizes are now real sizes, in millimetres. Smallest dot (starts at 0.5 mm) means no dot on the print is ever smaller than that, so every dot has enough white under it to take powder. Fainter parts get fewer dots of that size instead of tinier ones.
  • New: Smallest gap (starts at 0.4 mm). Where the holes between dots would be smaller than that, they would just fill in, so those spots print solid instead.
  • Dot test sheet. Click dot test sheet under the sliders to download a print-ready page of dots, holes and lines from 0.2 to 1.5 mm. Print it, see which sizes came out clean, and set the two sliders to match. Your settings are remembered.
  • Lines per inch now starts at 25 (dots about 1 mm apart), since 0.5 mm dots need room to grow. The hint under it shows the spacing and warns if the smallest dot is too big for it.
  • Before this, the smallest dot was a percentage, so at 50 lines per inch dots could be a fraction of a millimetre and the powder could not hold them.

0.1.2

  • Pick the shirt colour above the previews. One click on a swatch (black, white, heather, charcoal, navy, royal, red, maroon, forest, orange, gold, purple, pink, sand) or Other… for any colour. Both previews and the magnifier use it, and it remembers your last pick.
  • The magnifier always zooms in at least 3×, so it is obvious even on small files.

0.1.1

  • See the dots. Hover over either preview and a magnifier shows the same spot on both sides, with the real dots on the halftoned side. At Fit the dots blend together the way they do from across the room, which made it look like nothing had happened.
  • The empty part of each preview box is now a grey checkerboard, so it is not mistaken for part of the print.
  • Tip for Illustrator: a gradient to 0% opacity also fades its colour to whatever the 0% stop is set to, which is white by default. That prints as grey dots. Set the 0% stop's colour to the same colour as the solid end for a clean fade.

0.1.0

  • First version. Drop in a transparent PNG and the faded parts turn into solid ink dots that get smaller and further apart until they disappear into the shirt, like a screen print. Solid parts stay solid.
  • Why: DTF puts white under everything, so a see-through red prints pink. The file you download has no see-through pixels at all, every pixel is full ink or nothing, so the colour stays the real colour.
  • The faintest part of a fade does not stop at a line: the dots stop getting smaller and get fewer instead, so it trails off into scattered dots.
  • Side-by-side preview on your shirt colour. The left side can show the design as intended or how DTF prints it today (the pink halo).
  • Sliders for dot size (lines per inch), angle, the smallest dot worth printing, and how opaque counts as solid. Downloads a 600 DPI PNG by default, same print size. Nothing is uploaded; it all runs on your computer.
  • Lives in the employee portal under Other > Halftoner (needs BT Portal 0.60.0).
